canonical.title: Check for the power of 2
canonical.sourceFilePath: 06.Bit Manipulation/1. Learn Bit Manipulation/04.Check for the power of 2.cpp

narrative.title: Certifying the Cell Tower's Channel Count
narrative.scenario: A telecom planner can only deploy tower clusters whose channel counts are exact powers of two, because the switching fabric splits and merges channels in halves. A cluster size qualifies precisely when its binary form carries a single 1 bit. Subtracting one from such a number flips that lone bit and all lower bits, so one AND against the original exposes any impostor.
narrative.outputFormat: true when n is a positive power of two, false otherwise.

testCases.explanation: 16 is 10000 — one bit, four zeros, a clean 2^4.

hintLevels: Level 1: A power of two is the only positive integer whose binary form shows exactly one 1.
Level 2: n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit; on a true power of two that leaves zero.
Level 3: Guard n > 0 first — zero ANDs to zero with everything, and negatives would sneak past otherwise.
